Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: Double burden of malnutrition (overweight/obesity with vitamin D status) showed no significant association with depression or anxiety on the DASS-21.
Sentence: "No significant association was seen among DBM and DASS-21 outcomes."
Measured as: depression (DASS-21)
Population: 300 women aged 18-59 years with overweight or obesity attending health centres in Tehran
Intervention: Double burden of malnutrition (BMI >25 kg/m2 with plasma 25(OH)D concentration defined in the abstract as >20 ng/ml), measured not given
Comparator: Women without double burden of malnutrition
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 300
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Vitamin D deficiency was associated with abnormal HADS depression scores.
Sentence: "Deficient vitamin D and calcium consumption were associated with abnormal HADS scores for anxiety and depression (P < 0.05) and with increased severity of premenstrual headache, irritability, anxiety, and depression (P < 0.05)."
Measured as: HADS depression score
Population: 108 women with musculoskeletal pain and 108 healthy controls
Intervention: Serum vitamin D level (observational, deficient vs. non-deficient)
Comparator: Non-deficient vitamin D
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 216
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported
